Consult Summary:
Patient awoke at 05:30 today with a new, severe left-sided headache that persists despite paracetamol. Telephone assessment suggests probable migraine versus tension-type headache; management advice and follow-up arranged.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute severe left-sided headache (possible migraine vs tension headache)
- Onset: woke patient 05:30 today; still present.
- Character: unilateral (left), more intense than prior headaches (previously frontal, milder).
- Associated symptoms: mild photophobia; brief morning dizziness now resolved; no nausea, vomiting, fever, neck stiffness.
- Aggravating/relieving: wakes patient from sleep; initial discomfort lying down then slight relief; no relief with paracetamol.
- Pertinent negatives: no family history of migraine, no prior hypertension.
- Differential: migraine (unilateral, photophobia) vs tension headache (work stress).
- Plan: start ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) ± continue paracetamol; hydration 1.5-2 L/day, adequate sleep, read headache “red flag” information; urgent review if deterioration.

Issue 2: Chronic anxiety/stress related to work
- History: diagnosed anxiety ~2 years; on sertraline.
- Current stressors: heavy workload, late nights x 2 months; intermittent daytime frustration; denies current suicidal ideation.
- Plan: consider one week off work (self-certify); provide self-referral link to local counselling service; follow-up in one week.

Issue 3: Medication management
- Sertraline continued (dose not documented); no adverse effects reported.
- New recommendation: ibuprofen for headache; continue paracetamol if needed.
- Education on updated migraine first-line therapy and NSAID use.

Medications:
- Sertraline – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol – patient self-administered single dose (dose not documented) with minimal effect.
- Ibuprofen – advised to start (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Generalized anxiety disorder (≈2 years).

Social History:
- Lives with partner; owns a cat.
- Non-smoker.
- Runs ~3 times/week.
- Diet “OK”, not specifically healthy; alcohol intake not discussed.

Preventative History:
- No information on cancer screenings, vaccinations, or other preventive care.

Physical Examination:
- No in-person examination performed (telephone consult); vitals not obtained.

Plan:
- Begin ibuprofen for headache; may combine with paracetamol as needed.
- Ensure ≥7–8 h nightly sleep and 1.5–2 L non-caffeinated fluids daily.
- Take one week off work to reduce stress; self-certify sick leave.
- Provide counselling service self-referral link.
- Send patient written information on headache red-flag symptoms.
- Schedule follow-up appointment in 1 week; sooner if symptoms worsen or new concerns arise.
- Consider blood tests or further evaluation if no improvement at follow-up.

● No internal transcript conflicts noted.
